files.lesson.md: --- order: 10 unit: sci9 node: AC9M9M02 n1 uses: [AC9M9A01 n1] assumes: [AC9M8N02 n1, AC9M8N02 n2, AC9M9A01 n1] connection: sunlight-time title: Scientific notation summary: "Write a number as a number from 1 to 10 times a power of 10. Big numbers have a positive power and small numbers a negative one." language: maths voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } hook: "The speed of light has nine digits. Scientists write it in a few characters instead." app: command: node "$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs" "$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground-board" 8347 url: http://127.0.0.1:8347/index.html readySelector: "#gsum" layout: full explainPicture: { ref: sci.yml#explain-pic, caption: "$3 \\times 10^8$: the decimal point of 3 moves 8 places right, giving 300 000 000." } explainClip: query: { code: "@sci.yml#explain", fresh: 1, id: explain } caption: "The power says how far the point moves" say: "The power of ten says how far the decimal point moves, and which way." clip: - caption: { text: "4.5 × 10⁰ = 4.5: the point stays.", say: "With power zero the point stays where it is." } - click: Make k bigger - click: Make k bigger - click: Make k bigger - wait: 900 - caption: { text: "4.5 × 10³ = 4 500: the point moves 3 right.", say: "Power three: the point moves three places right." } - click: Make k smaller - click: Make k smaller - click: Make k smaller - click: Make k smaller - click: Make k smaller - click: Make k smaller - wait: 900 - caption: { text: "4.5 × 10⁻³ = 0.0045: the point moves 3 left.", say: "Power minus three: the point moves three places left." } - wait: 800 --- Some numbers are too long to read. Scientific notation puts the length in a power of 10 instead. ## Predict: the speed of light ```step stage: predict insight: "Committing to a power for 300 000 000 shows who counts the zeros wrongly, or gives a big number a negative power." check: type: predict q: "Light travels at about 300 000 000 metres per second. Which is that in scientific notation?" options: - "$3 \\times 10^{8}$" - "$3 \\times 10^{9}$" - "$3 \\times 10^{7}$" - "$3 \\times 10^{-8}$" actual: "3 × 10⁸. The decimal point moves 8 places from 3 to 300 000 000. There are 8 zeros. A big number has a positive power; 3 × 10⁻⁸ would be 0.00000003." ``` The speed of light is about 300 000 000 m/s. How can you write it with a short power of 10? ## Run: move the point ```step stage: run insight: "The power of 10 says how many places the decimal point moves and which way: right for a positive power, left for a negative one." try: { playground: board, starter: "sci.yml#run", height: 600 } check: { type: board, text: "Set the board to $3 \\times 10^{8}$ (change $a$ to 3 and $k$ to 8). What does it write out? Was your prediction right?", when: "a = 3 and k = 8" } ``` The first number $a$ is from 1 to 9.9. The board writes the number out for you. Try a negative $k$ too. ## Investigate: big and small ```step stage: investigate insight: "The number part must be from 1 up to 10. Count how far the decimal point moves: right for a big number (positive power), left for a small one (negative power). Ravi counts the wrong way for a small number." tasks: - check: type: number q: "Write $45\\,000$ as $4.5 \\times 10^{k}$. What's $k$?" answer: 4 explain: "The point moves 4 places, from 4.5 to 45 000. So k = 4." - check: type: bug code: "working.txt#ravi" text: "Ravi writes 0.0004 in scientific notation. Click the line where his working goes wrong." answer: 3 fault: logic misconception: sci-notation-places explain: "Line 3: the point moves 4 places to the left, and a small number has a negative power: 4 × 10⁻⁴." - check: type: question q: "Which one is in scientific notation?" options: ["$1.2 \\times 10^{4}$", "$12 \\times 10^{3}$", "$0.12 \\times 10^{5}$", "$120 \\times 10^{2}$"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "The first number must be less than 10: 12 is too big.", "The first number must be at least 1: 0.12 is too small.", "The first number must be less than 10: 120 is too big."] explain: "All four are 12 000. Only 1.2 × 10⁴ has a number from 1 up to 10." ``` ### How far Here's converting both ways. ```worked 45\,000 :: A big number. 4.5 \times 10^{4} :: The point moves 4 places left to sit after the 4: a positive power. 0.00072 :: A small number. 7.2 \times 10^{-4} :: The point moves 4 places right, to sit after the 7: a negative power. 3.6 \times 10^{5} = 360\,000 :: Back again: move the point 5 places right. ``` Now try one on paper: $0.000\,038$ in scientific notation. Then type the power. ### Find the mistake Read Ravi's working. Which way does the point move for a small number? ### Which is scientific notation? ## Modify: change the number ```step stage: modify insight: "One change at a time: a bigger number, then back to a decimal, then a power of zero." try: { playground: board, starter: "sci.yml#vary", height: 620 } tasks: - hint: ["The board shows the number written out.", "Set a to 6.3 and find the k that writes 6 300 000."] check: { type: number, q: "Write $6\\,300\\,000$ as $6.3 \\times 10^{k}$. What's $k$?", answer: 6, explain: "The point moves 6 places: k = 6." } smaller: check: { type: "number", q: "How many places does the point move from 6.3 to 6 300 000?", answer: 6, explain: "6.3 → 63 → 630 → 6 300 → 63 000 → 630 000 → 6 300 000: six places." } - hint: ["A negative power: the point moves left.", "$5.1 \\times 10^{-3}$ is a small number."] check: { type: answer, q: "Write $5.1 \\times 10^{-3}$ as a decimal.", answer: "0.0051", form: simplified, feedback: [["5100", "A negative power makes a small number, not a big one."], ["0.051", "Three places left, not two: 0.0051."]], explain: "The point moves 3 places left: 0.0051." } - hint: ["$10^0 = 1$.", "So the point doesn't move."] check: { type: answer, q: "Edge case: write $7.2 \\times 10^{0}$ as a decimal.", answer: "7.2", form: simplified, feedback: [["72", "10⁰ = 1, so the point doesn't move."]], explain: "10⁰ = 1, so 7.2 × 1 = 7.2." } ``` ### A bigger number ### Back to a decimal ### Power zero ## Practise: both ways ```step stage: practise insight: "Converting big and small numbers both ways, mixed; the review keeps negative powers fresh." tasks: - check: type: number q: "Write $82\\,000\\,000$ as $8.2 \\times 10^{k}$. What's $k$?" answer: 7 explain: "The point moves 7 places: k = 7." - check: type: number q: "Write $0.000\\,52$ as $5.2 \\times 10^{k}$. What's $k$?" answer: -4 explain: "The point moves 4 places left past the zeros: k = −4." smaller: check: { type: "number", q: "How many places does the point move from 0.000 52 to 5.2?", answer: 4, explain: "0.00052 → 0.0052 → 0.052 → 0.52 → 5.2: four places. It moves right, so the power is negative: −4." } - check: type: answer q: "Write $9.4 \\times 10^{5}$ as a number." answer: "940000" form: simplified feedback: - ["94000", "Five places right: 940 000."] explain: "The point moves 5 places right: 940 000." - check: type: answer q: "Review: work out $10^{-4}$ as a decimal." answer: "0.0001" form: simplified feedback: - ["0.001", "10⁻⁴ = 1/10 000."] explain: "10⁻⁴ = 1/10 000 = 0.0001." ``` ### A big number ### A small number ### Back to a number ### Review A negative power, from earlier. ## Make: back to the speed of light ```step stage: make insight: "Coming back to the opening: writing a long number in scientific notation shows its size at a glance." tasks: - hint: ["299 792 458 is close to 300 000 000.", "How many places does the point move?"] check: type: reasoning paper: true q: "Light travels at 299 792 458 m/s. Round it to $3 \\times 10^{k}$ m/s. What's $k$? Then say how many times faster it is than a car at $3 \\times 10^{1}$ m/s." steps: - ["$299\\,792\\,458 \\approx 300\\,000\\,000$", "round to one digit"] - ["$300\\,000\\,000 = 3 \\times 10^{8}$", "the point moves 8 places"] - ["$(3 \\times 10^{8}) \\div (3 \\times 10^{1}) = 10^{7}$", "divide the numbers, subtract the powers"] answer: "8" answerLabel: "The power k" feedback: - ["9", "300 000 000 has 8 zeros, so the point moves 8 places."] - ["-8", "A big number has a positive power."] criteria: - "I rounded before writing it in scientific notation." - "My number part is from 1 to 10." - "The speed of light is a big number, so my power is positive." explain: "3 × 10⁸ m/s. A car at 3 × 10¹ m/s (about 108 km/h) is 10⁷, ten million, times slower." - check: type: number q: "Which is smaller, $3 \\times 10^{-5}$ or $3 \\times 10^{-7}$? Type the power of the smaller one." answer: -7 explain: "3 × 10⁻⁷ = 0.0000003 is smaller than 3 × 10⁻⁵ = 0.00003." ``` ### The power of light Back to light. Work it out on paper first, then type the power. ### Which is smaller? Speed of light: 299 792 458 m/s, exact: [NIST](https://physics.nist.gov/cuu/Constants/Value/c.html). **Also used in** - **Space and science.** Sizes from atoms to galaxies are written this way. - **Next lesson.** Calculating with numbers in scientific notation, like how far the Sun is. ```teacher summary: Students write numbers in scientific notation with a number part from 1 to 10, see the decimal point move left or right on a board, and avoid the sign slip on small numbers (AC9M9M02, node 1). time: 40 timing: Predict and Run 8 min · Investigate 12 min · Modify 10 min · Practise and Make 10 min goals: - I can write a big number in scientific notation. - I can write a small number in scientific notation with a negative power. - I can turn scientific notation back into a decimal. struggle: "The sign of the power for small numbers. Ask students: did the point move right (a negative power) or left?" before: > Do the Run board yourself first. Students need Negative powers. This is a hinge lesson: exponent sign errors on small numbers corrupt everything after it. The common mistake is a positive power for a small number (Ravi's working). The speed of light, 299 792 458 m/s, is exact (NIST). The lesson rounds it to 3 × 10⁸ for the task. running: - "Predict: take a show of hands. Those who chose 3 × 10⁹ counted the digits (9) rather than the zeros or the moves." - "Run: ask students to say which way the point moves before they press the slider." - "Paper: the try-one after the worked example and the speed of light in Make are worked on paper first. Books out, and look for an arrow showing which way the point moved." - "Modify: before 5.1 × 10⁻³, ask if the number is bigger or smaller than 1." stuck: - see: A student writes 0.0004 = 4 × 10⁴. ask: Is 0.0004 bigger or smaller than 1? fix: "Smaller, so the power is negative: 4 × 10⁻⁴." - see: A student writes 12 × 10³ as scientific notation. ask: Is 12 between 1 and 10? fix: "No: 1.2 × 10⁴." stretch: Why does the number part have to be from 1 to 10? What goes wrong if it doesn't? support: A strip with the decimal point and an arrow, and a number line of powers of 10 from 10⁻⁵ to 10⁵. leads: > Starts AC9M9M02. Where it leads: calculating with scientific notation (next), measurements in science and medicine. exit: q: Write 0.0072 in scientific notation. a: 7.2 × 10⁻³. explain: > Scientific notation is a number from 1 up to (but not including) 10, times a power of 10. Big numbers have a positive power: $45\,000 = 4.5 \times 10^4$. Small numbers have a negative power: $0.0072 = 7.2 \times 10^{-3}$. The power says how many places the decimal point moves. ```

files.working.txt:
# Ravi's working for the "find the mistake" task. Plain text: students click the wrong line, nothing runs.

# region: ravi
Write 0.0004 in scientific notation.
The first digit is 4, so the number part is 4.
The point moves 4 places, so the power is 4.
So 0.0004 = 4 × 10⁴.
# endregion
